note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, after 66858fa127). RFC 7606 Section 3 (j): "If this is not possible, the procedures of [RFC4271] and/or [RFC4760] continue to apply, meaning that the "session reset" approach (or the "AFI/SAFI disable" approach) MUST be followed." Changed unit: TestRFC7606MPUnreachTooShort now requires the exact description "RFC 7606 Section 5.3: MP_UNREACH_NLRI length 2 < 3" besides exact SessionReset and AttrCode 15; its buffer (ORIGIN, empty AS_PATH, MP_UNREACH length 2 carrying AFI only) cannot be parsed, and the exact text pins the outcome to validateMPAttrLength (rfc7606.go), which returns before validateMPNLRIField could index the missing SAFI. The claim states what the body checks. Re-read the other negatives: MP_REACH length 4 (exact SessionReset, code 14), IPv4 /33 and NLRI overrun through ValidateNLRISyntax (exact SessionReset), IPv6 /129 through the production MP path (exact SessionReset, "129 > 128"), plus the unchanged session-level TestEnforceRFC7606_InvalidTrailingNLRI and the wire-level rfc7606-reset.ci. Positives (parseable IPv4 and IPv6 NLRI give nil) show the reset is not applied to a field that parses. Ze implements the session-reset alternative, which satisfies the MUST. Not verdict-changing: the positives are function-level and prove only that a parseable field is not reset; the other half of 3(j)'s spirit (a parseable NLRI with an attribute error gets treat-as-withdraw) is proven under the 7.x rows, not here. Verdict stands.
